answer: Randomized Assignment Lottery works by routing each new agent's first tasks through a public beacon whose seed is fixed only after the agent registers. The scheduler draws assignments from that seed across a wide knoll of task pools, so an attacker cannot predict or cluster placements before committing. Because the seed locks post-registration, farms cannot precompute favorable routes or concentrate sybils on cheap queues.
